title: Toyota Recalls Certain Model Year 2022-2023 and 2025-2026 Toyota Tundra Vehicles

body_markdown:
**PLANO, Texas (Nov. 13, 2026)** — Toyota is conducting a safety recall involving certain model year 2022-2023 and 2025-2026 Tundra non-hybrid vehicles. Approximately 62,000 vehicles are involved in this recall in the U.S.


The subject vehicles could be equipped with an engine camshaft that was manufactured incorrectly, which could snap during driving. This can lead to a loss of motive power at higher speeds, increasing the risk of a crash.


Affected camshafts are from one specific production lot from a specific supplier. We estimate that there are approximately 300 affected camshafts that could have been installed in the subject vehicles.


All known owners of the subject vehicles will be notified to return their vehicle to a Toyota dealer. The dealer will inspect the camshaft to see if it may be from the affected lot and, if so, the camshaft will be replaced at no cost to the customer.


Owners of involved vehicles will be notified by mid-January 2027.


Information about automotive recalls, including but not limited to the list of involved vehicles, is current as of today’s filing date and is subject to change thereafter. To see if your vehicle is involved in a safety recall visit Toyota.com/recall or nhtsa.gov/recalls and enter your Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) or license plate information.


For any additional questions, Toyota customer support is also available by calling the Toyota Brand Engagement Center (1-800-331-4331).
